keyframe_review.note: The Wikipedia title Cliopatria gives, 'Arab Iraq', is a geographical term ('a historical geographical term used by medieval and early modern writers for the region of Iraq'), not a state, and the page never mentions a federation. The real Hashemite Arab Federation lasted 14 February - 2 August 1958 (Arab Federation page). The shape (222,000 km2: Basra, Wasit, Dhi Qar, Maysan, Babil, Qadisiyyah, Karbala, 73% of Khuzestan and part of Kuwait) is the Jalayirid remnant in lower Iraq: after 1410 'pushed into lower Iraq (Hillah, Wasit, Basra)', capital Hillah then Basra (1411-1432), eliminated by the Qara Qoyunlu in 1432 (Jalayirid page). The jalayirid-sultanate dossier already has the keyframes 1410-1422 and 1423-1432; do not draw this row.

correction.text: lower Iraq: Jalayirid to 1432 (jalayirid-sultanate_1423), Qara Qoyunlu from 1432

keyframe_review.note: Same row, 1431-1439: the Jalayirid page has the Qara Qoyunlu prince Aspan capture al-Hilla in October 1431, the last Jalayirid ruler Hosayn II killed on 9 November 1431 and the dynasty 'finally eliminated by the Qara Qoyunlu in 1432'. For 1432-1439 the same lower Iraq is Qara Qoyunlu land (the qara-qoyunlu dossier has the 1432 gain, and its 1440 Cliopatria shape includes Basra and Wasit). Nothing called a federation exists.

correction.text: Iraq and Jordan with the West Bank, the Kingdom of Iraq plus the Hashemite Kingdom

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the real federation. Infobox area 533,314 km2 against the gazetteer's 511,000 km2 for Iraq, Jordan and the West Bank (ratio 0.96). As a confederation that 'united foreign policy and defense of each country but left the vast majority of other domestic programs under national jurisdiction' it is an association: the extent is kept for the state page and is not coloured as territory (rule 4, umbrella). Cliopatria's Kingdom of Iraq row ends in 1957 and its Iraqi Republic row begins in 1960, so the two kingdoms' own shapes for 1958-1959 are a matter for those dossiers.

region.text: Iraq and Jordan with the West Bank, the Kingdom of Iraq plus the Hashemite Kingdom

ledger.note: 14 February 1958: King Faisal II of Iraq and his cousin King Hussein of Jordan unite their kingdoms in the Arab Federation 'as a response to the formation of the United Arab Republic'; Nuri al-Said becomes 'Premier of the Arab Union'. Infobox 'Established: 14 February 1958', capital Baghdad.
14 July 1958: Faisal II is deposed in the military coup of Abd al-Karim Qasim ('overthrow the government there in the 14 July Revolution'); Iraq leaves the federation in all but name.

region.text: Iraq and Jordan with the West Bank, the Kingdom of Iraq plus the Hashemite Kingdom

ledger.note: 2 August 1958: the new Iraqi government officially dissolves the federation (infobox 'Disestablished: 2 August 1958'); Jordan carries on as the Hashemite Kingdom.

wars.name: 14 July Revolution
belligerents: Free Officers of Abd al-Karim Qasim
wars.outcome: Qasim's troops overthrow the government in Baghdad on 14 July 1958 and the Iraqi government dissolves the federation on 2 August; not a war over borders, listed so the reviewer can see it was considered.
wars.note: The page mentions the coup in one sentence; a 14 July Revolution article was not opened.

certainty.note: The two kingdoms' own frontiers were fixed; the union itself drew no border and is not coloured as territory.

notes:
The Cliopatria row 'Hashemite Arab Federation' (1415-1439, Wikipedia title 'Arab Iraq', Wikidata Q6000379) is a mis-labelled shape of lower Iraq in the 15th century: the Jalayirid remnant to 1432 and then Qara Qoyunlu land. The Arab Iraq article is a geographical term and mentions no state or federation. This dossier therefore marks both Cliopatria shapes 'wrong' and writes the real Hashemite Arab Federation of 1958 (14 February - 2 August) from the Arab Federation article. Wikidata Q6000379 is Cliopatria's id for the 'Arab Iraq' page and is probably the region, not the 1958 federation; Wikidata is unreachable, so unchecked. The identity's Wikipedia field names the Arab Federation article (the article's own infobox and text call it 'Hashemite Arab Federation' and 'Arab Union or Arab Federation'); Cliopatria's 'Arab Iraq' is not the federation.
Type umbrella: the page calls it a 'confederal constitutional diarchy' which 'united foreign policy and defense of each country but left the vast majority of other domestic programs under national jurisdiction'; the two kingdoms keep their own territory and the map should not colour the federation.
Colour and rendering agents: delete the 1415-1439 shapes of this row for those years (their land is covered by jalayirid-sultanate_1410/_1423 and the Qara Qoyunlu dossier); the row now has meaning only in 1958.
Gaps for other dossiers: (1) Cliopatria's Kingdom of Iraq ends in 1957 and its Iraqi Republic starts in 1960, leaving Iraq without a shape for 1958-1959; the Arab Federation page has the monarchy to the coup of 14 July 1958. (2) The Cliopatria Hashemite shape adds Khuzestan (73%) and Kuwait to lower Iraq; the Jalayirid page puts Shushtar in Khuzestan under the Jalayirids to 1423 (the jalayirid-sultanate dossier carries it). (3) The page gives no ruler list for the union, so no ruler strip.
Pages opened: Arab Iraq, Arab Federation, and the Jalayirid Sultanate page shared with the Qara Qoyunlu and Muzaffarid dossiers. Gazetteer: every name resolves.
